title: Pro-etale extension-by-zero base change
statement:
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X
\end{array}
$$

be an open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]
and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. For every complex
$K$ of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $U_{\Proet}$ the canonical map

$$
g^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!g_U^{-1}K
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $K$; here all functors are the
pro-etale ones of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], with inverse image as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and the small sites and constant-coefficient derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

proof.text: Work first with sheaves of modules over the constant coefficient rings. The construction [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] gives morphisms of topoi for $g$ and $g_U$. Their coefficient structure maps $c^g_\Lambda,c^{g_U}_\Lambda$ are isomorphisms preserving constant sections by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Hence the tensor-formula module pullbacks identify with the inverse images denoted $g^{-1},g_U^{-1}$: after transporting scalars through $c$, the maps $r\otimes m\mapsto rm$ and $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ are inverse. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] gives the module adjunctions $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ and $g_U^{-1}\dashv g_{U*}$.

For either $e:W\hookrightarrow Z$ equal to $j$ or $j'$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$ and identifies the restricted constant coefficient ring with $\Lambda_W$. We check from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] that $e^{-1}$ is restriction. At a site object $T\to W$, the inverse-image indexing category has the initial object $(T,T\to W\times_ZT)$. Indeed an object $(V,\phi:T\to W\times_ZV)$ gives the unique $Z$-arrow $T\to V$ by projection; its compatibility with $\phi$ follows by comparing the two projections. The opposite indexing category therefore has this object terminal, so the presheaf colimit is $F(T\to Z)$. These values are already a sheaf, by the site equivalence. For $T_1\to T_2$ the colimit maps become the restrictions $F(T_2)\to F(T_1)$, so this identifies functors. The coefficient identification preserves constant sections and therefore identifies the scalar actions too. This proves the assertion simultaneously for both open immersions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] to $j$ and $j'$, with the given finite commutative ring $\Lambda$. In the restriction coordinates of step 2 this supplies $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ and $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ on module sheaves, and both extension-by-zero functors are exact and act degreewise on complexes. All four adjunctions now have the constant-coefficient module categories as their domains and codomains.

source.place: Tag 09AE, definition-extension-zero (3); blueprint proof, first paragraph

proof.text:
The cartesian datum of [def-cbc-open-immersion-square] gives, for every $V\to U$, an isomorphism
$$a_V:V\times_UU'\xrightarrow{\sim}V\times_XX'.$$
Its projections send $(v,u')$ to $(v,j'(u'))$. Conversely a compatible pair $(v,x')$ determines the unique $u'$ whose images are the image of $v$ in $U$ and $x'$ in $X'$, by the given fibre-product universal property. The two composites fix both projections and so are identities. The same uniqueness shows these maps commute with each arrow $V_1\to V_2$ over $U$. Thus the localization of the base-change functor for $g$ at $U$ identifies with the base-change functor for $g_U$, under the site identifications of step 2.

source.place: Second paragraph, identification of the two base-changed weakly etale objects

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] to the continuous base-change functor $u_g$, with $V=U$ and $u_g(U)\cong U'$. Its smallness, continuity and finite-limit hypotheses hold by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; its ring map is the constant-coefficient map of step 1. The localized ring map agrees with that for $g_U$: their adjuncts both send $\lambda\in\Lambda$ to the constant section $\lambda$ after base change, and maps from the constant presheaf extend uniquely to its sheafification. In the module and site coordinates of steps 1, 2 and 4, the cited theorem therefore gives
$$t:j^{-1}g_*\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{U*}j'^{-1}.$$
More explicitly, for a module sheaf $M$ on $X'_{\mathrm{proet}}$,
$$(j^{-1}g_*M)(V)=M(V\times_XX'),\qquad(g_{U*}j'^{-1}M)(V)=M(V\times_UU'),$$
and $t_{M,V}=M(a_V)$ with inverse $M(a_V^{-1})$. Naturality in $V$ follows from step 4, and naturality in $M$ from functoriality. Linearity for the restricted $\Lambda_U(V)$-action is included in the ringed localization theorem. Thus this is the canonical natural isomorphism of right adjoints, without imposing strict equality on chosen fibre products or skeleta.

Set $L_1=g^{-1}j_!$, $R_1=j^{-1}g_*$, $L_2=j'_!g_U^{-1}$ and $R_2=g_{U*}j'^{-1}$. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and steps 1 and 3 there are composite adjunctions $L_1\dashv R_1$ and $L_2\dashv R_2$. Their Hom bijections are, respectively,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(g^{-1}j_!F,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!F,g_*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,j^{-1}g_*M),$$
$$\operatorname{Hom}(j'_!g_U^{-1}F,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(g_U^{-1}F,j'^{-1}M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,g_{U*}j'^{-1}M).$$
Let $\delta=t^{-1}:R_2\xrightarrow{\sim}R_1$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] gives a natural isomorphism $\beta:L_1\xrightarrow{\sim}L_2$, characterized by
$$R_1(\beta_F)\circ\eta_{1,F}=\delta_{L_2F}\circ\eta_{2,F}.$$
Here the units are those of the displayed composite adjunctions. To specify the comparison, not merely the existence of some isomorphism, its component is explicitly
$$\beta_F=\varepsilon_{1,L_2F}\circ L_1(\delta_{L_2F})\circ L_1(\eta_{2,F}).$$
The adjoint of this map is $\delta_{L_2F}\circ\eta_{2,F}$, by the adjunction triangle identity. This is exactly the unit/counit construction of the open extension-by-zero base-change map in the direction of the statement, conjugating the sectionwise cartesian comparison $t^{-1}$. The reverse comparison is
$$\gamma_F=\varepsilon_{2,L_1F}\circ L_2(t_{L_1F})\circ L_2(\eta_{1,F}).$$
The cited conjugation theorem applied in the reverse direction, and its uniqueness under the unit equation, show $\gamma=\beta^{-1}$. Thus the canonical comparison, with this orientation, is invertible and natural in $F$.

proof.text: For the additional normalized constant-ring module interface singleBetaInv, use the fixed-scalar realization C with coefficient map the identity. Its scalar map is an isomorphism: after precomposing with the locally bijective constant unit it is the locally bijective finite scalar map. Thus C is an equivalence. Its sectionwise direct-image comparison, followed by uniqueness of left adjoints, identifies module pullback and open extension with the ordinary fixed-scalar operations. The weakly-etale base-change isomorphism for the two open immersions, conjugated under the two composite adjunctions, therefore places g^{-1}j_!M in the essential image of jprime_!. The ordinary open unit is invertible by the localization adjoint triple; transport along C makes both module open units invertible. Fully faithfulness of jprime_! now makes its counit invertible at g^{-1}j_!M. Expanding the original, unchanged singleBetaInvApp by the adjunction counit formula expresses it as jprime_! applied to the pulled-back open unit and moduleSquareG inverse, followed by this counit. Each factor is invertible, so every component of this particular comparison is invertible. This argument needs only the essential-image consequence of the transported comparison, and does not choose a replacement comparison.

source.place: Tag 09AE, extension by zero on the localized site; constant-scalar coordinate transport and the fully faithful adjunction criterion.

proof.text:
For a cochain complex $K$, take in degree $n$ the sheaf isomorphism $\beta_{K^n}$ constructed in step 6. Naturality with respect to $d^n:K^n\to K^{n+1}$ says
$$L_2(d^n)\circ\beta_{K^n}=\beta_{K^{n+1}}\circ L_1(d^n).$$
Consequently these components form a chain map $L_1K\to L_2K$. Naturality of $\gamma$ gives $L_1(d^n)\circ\gamma_{K^n}=\gamma_{K^{n+1}}\circ L_2(d^n)$, so its components form the reverse chain map. The two composites in degree $n$ are $\gamma_{K^n}\circ\beta_{K^n}=\mathrm{id}_{L_1K^n}$ and $\beta_{K^n}\circ\gamma_{K^n}=\mathrm{id}_{L_2K^n}$. Naturality for a map of complexes holds in each degree by step 6. This proves the asserted natural isomorphism on complexes, without any boundedness or constructibility assumption.

source.place: Proof, concluding assertion for complexes; the degreewise chain-map verification is written out here

proof.text: If $K$ is read as an object of the ordinary unbounded derived category, the same comparison applies. The functors $g^{-1}$ and $g_U^{-1}$ on the finite constant-coefficient module sheaves are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]; the functors $j_!$ and $j'_!$ are exact and act degreewise by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] each of these termwise functors preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces its exact derived functor, represented by its termwise value on every complex. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], clause (2), to the natural chain isomorphisms $\beta$ and $\gamma$ of step 7, composed with the target localization. They descend to inverse natural transformations because their compositions and the identity transformations descend compatibly. This is the same canonical comparison on the derived category, and it is an isomorphism there as well. No ordinary $g_*$ is being substituted for $Rg_*$ in a derived Hom calculation: the right-adjoint argument was completed on sheaves before taking complexes and localizing.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; natural transformations descend by the localization universal property, as stated in the cited DAG node
